sources.title: RIT CSCI-605 Advanced Object-Oriented Programming Concepts catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: This course focuses on identifying advanced object-oriented programming concepts and implementing them in the context of specific problems. This course covers advanced concepts such as event-driven programming, design patterns, distributed and concurrent programming, and the use, design and implementation of applications. Assignments (both in class and as homework) requiring a solution to a problem and an implementation in code are an integral part of the course. Note: This course serves as a bridge course for graduate students and cannot be taken by undergraduate students without permission from the CS Undergraduate Program Coordinator. This course is restricted to students in COMPSCI-MS. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Fall, Spring

sources.title: Java Language Specification
sources.author: Oracle
sources.content: The Java language specification defines classes, objects, interfaces, inheritance, method invocation, fields, access control, exceptions, generics, and concurrency semantics. A class declares state and behavior, while an object is an instance with its own runtime identity and field state. Interfaces declare contracts that classes may implement. Inheritance reuses and specializes behavior, but dynamic method dispatch selects an implementation from the runtime class of the receiver. Access modifiers control which declarations are visible. Exceptions separate normal results from abrupt completion. Generic types express reusable abstractions while preserving compile-time type constraints. Object-oriented design should make responsibilities, invariants, dependencies, composition, and substitution behavior explicit.

sources.title: Python Data Model
sources.author: Python Software Foundation
sources.content: Python objects have identity, a type, and a value. Classes create user-defined types whose instances can contain attributes and participate in operations through special methods. Attribute lookup follows defined rules across an instance and its class hierarchy. Methods bind functions to instances. Inheritance allows a class to derive behavior from base classes, while composition connects objects through explicit attributes. Mutable and immutable objects have different state behavior. Exceptions communicate failures through defined control flow. A sound object model states ownership, invariants, public operations, extension points, and observable behavior rather than relying on hidden shared state.
